summary: Lookout tower named Fort Benning in Chattahoochee County, listed at 493 (read as feet). A federal survey station has a destroyed-mark entry; no source describes the tower today.

facts.status_note: No source confirms that a tower stands here; a federal survey entry for its station reports a destroyed surface mark.

access.note: The name is that of an Army post, and most of Chattahoochee County has been part of the Fort Benning military reservation since 1918. No source describes public access to this tower.

corrections.why: The index the record was built from spells the county Chatahoochee. The county's Wikipedia page spells it Chattahoochee, so the index spelling is a typo.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Sources are the state tower index, an NGS station listing, a Forest Lookouts Georgia list and Wikipedia. None gives a build date, builder, design, staffing, fires or fate. The index's elevation column is read as feet, which matches the metre value in the record. NGS station CM1885 appears twice with codes XX and NN and no date; it is a survey mark, not the tower, and the two codes are not reconciled. The index also lists 'fort benning S' and 'fort benning E' from 1950 Army topographic maps; the story does not say whether they are separate towers. The 1995 Garrow and Associates Historic Preservation Plan, Vol. 2 (UGA report 14160) was read only as its abstract; the full volume may cover fire towers on the post and is worth checking. Story is about 186 words.
